title: Comparing and Grouping Rocks
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Comparing and Grouping Rocks Worksheets (Igneous, Sedimentary, Metamorphic)
standard_text: Compare and group together different kinds of rocks on the basis of their appearance and simple physical properties.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on rocks: grouping rocks by appearance and properties, hardness and permeability tests, igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks, and uses of rocks. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks form in different ways.
body_html:
How to think about it

We group rocks by how they look and how they behave.

  • Look for grains, crystals, layers, holes and colour. Test hardness with a scratch test and whether water soaks in.
  • Igneous rocks form from melted rock; sedimentary rocks form from layers; metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure.
  • Bricks, concrete and glass are man-made, not natural rocks.
Example

Water soaks into chalk. It is?

Water goes in

Answer: permeable

Example

Slate is used for roofs because?

Waterproof thin sheets

Answer: it is impermeable and splits into flat sheets

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all rocks are hard.
  • Thinking bricks and concrete are rocks.
  • Thinking shiny rocks are always the hardest.

faq.a: By how they look (grains, crystals, layers, colour) and by simple tests: how hard they are and whether water soaks in.

faq.q: What are the three types of rock?
faq.a: Igneous rocks form when melted rock cools. Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sand, mud or shells. Metamorphic rocks are rocks changed by heat and pressure.
A permeable rock lets water soak into it, like chalk or sandstone. An impermeable rock does not, like slate or granite.
